title: India's surprise baby bust
summary: India's fertility rate has dropped sharply to 1.78 children per woman in 2024, falling below replacement level much faster than demographers predicted. This 'baby bust' signals a major demographic shift that will reshape the nation's economy and serves as a warning to other developing countries following similar fertility trajectories.
problem_solved: Highlights the unexpected speed of demographic transition in India and its economic implications for workforce and aging population.
why_valuable: Provides critical insights into how rapidly developing nations can transition through demographic stages, offering policy lessons for managing aging populations and economic planning.
